tagline: From the Angola gate along an old portage through the hills.
intro: Highway 66 starts at the main gate of the Louisiana State Penitentiary at Angola, in a bend of the Mississippi near the state line, and winds about 20 miles through the wooded Tunica Hills to US 61 at Bains, north of St. Francisville. It follows an ancient Native American portage called the Tunica Trace, and burial mounds lie in the country around it.
The road has been straightened in places by cutting into the hills. At Tunica the curve it left behind is still there, now called Crescent Road.
season: Spring, when flowers bloom along the way.

moments.title: Angola
moments.text: The prison covers 28 square miles of Isaac Franklin's old slave plantations, one named Angola for the African country many of the enslaved came from, and it still runs as a working farm.

moments.title: Tunica Hills Wildlife Management Area
moments.text: The highway runs between the two tracts of forested bluffs and ravines, home to birds rare elsewhere in Louisiana, such as the worm-eating warbler and the Cooper's hawk.

moments.title: Big Bayou Sara
moments.text: After following the snaking Little Bayou Sara for several miles, the road turns east and crosses the main bayou on a pony truss bridge from the 1940s.
